label: Logical neutrality versus physical basis and practical selection
term: logical neutrality versus physical basis and practical selection
resolution: A recoding is a reversible representation change, not a physical process. The fixed evidence condition and equivariance are separate assumptions. Set-valued answer is not a probability or practical action. Absence of a unique neutral answer does not imply irrational induction or forbid a basis-sensitive choice. Original-coordinate uniformity and recoded-coordinate uniformity are distinct added criteria, not syntactic measures of physical naturalness. The two complete predictions are a bounded green/grue-type profile, not an attributed definition of Goodman grue.
